NumberWordFormatter.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initialize five instance lookup-table lists for number words, teen words, tens words, large-number scale names, and abbreviated suffixes using fixed string constants." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER to a 10-element literal list mapping index 0 to an empty string and indices 1 through 9 to the uppercase single-digit words ONE through NINE. RESULT self.NUMBER]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_TEEN to a 10-element literal list mapping indices 0 through 9 to the uppercase teen words TEN through NINETEEN. RESULT self.NUMBER_TEEN]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_TEN to a 9-element literal list mapping indices 0 through 8 to the uppercase tens words TEN, TWENTY, THIRTY, FORTY, FIFTY, SIXTY, SEVENTY, EIGHTY, and NINETY. RESULT self.NUMBER_TEN]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_MORE to a 4-element literal list mapping index 0 to an empty string and indices 1 through 3 to the uppercase scale names THOUSAND, MILLION, and BILLION. RESULT self.NUMBER_MORE]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_SUFFIX to a 16-element literal list containing the exact suffix sequence k, w, empty string, m, empty string, empty string, b, empty string, empty string, t, empty string, empty string, p, empty string, empty string, and e. RESULT self.NUMBER_SUFFIX]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.format:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Return a formatted string for x when x is not None, otherwise return an empty string." format]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance providing the format_string method."
        <REF> x </REF>: any "Value to format if it is not None."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "Formatted string for x, or an empty string when x is None."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether x is not None. RESULT condition]
            [COMMAND If x is not None, convert x to a string and pass it to self.format_string, then return the formatted result. RESULT formatted_value]
            [COMMAND If x is None, return an empty string. RESULT empty_string]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.format_string:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Formats a numeric string with optional cents into a spelled-out amount, returning ZERO ONLY when the whole-number part is blank or zero." format_string]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance providing number-to-words conversion helpers."
        <REF> x </REF>: string "Input amount string, optionally containing a decimal point."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "Formatted uppercase amount text ending with ONLY."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Split x on the first dot, pad with an empty string, and assign the first part to lstr and the second part to rstr; then reverse lstr into lstrrev and initialize a as a list of five empty strings. RESULT lstr, rstr, lstrrev, a]
            [COMMAND If the length of lstrrev modulo 3 equals 1, append two zeros to lstrrev; otherwise, if the length modulo 3 equals 2, append one zero to lstrrev; otherwise leave it unchanged. RESULT lstrrev]
            [COMMAND Initialize lm as an empty string. RESULT lm]
            [COMMAND Within the loop over i from 0 up to but not including len(lstrrev) // 3, take the 3-character slice at positions 3*i through 3*i+2, reverse it, and store it in a[i]. RESULT a[i]]
            [COMMAND Within the same loop, if a[i] is not equal to 000, prepend the text from self.trans_three(a[i]) and self.parse_more(i) to lm; otherwise append only the text from self.trans_three(a[i]) to lm. RESULT lm]
            [COMMAND Build xs as AND CENTS followed by self.trans_two(rstr) and a trailing space when rstr is nonempty; otherwise set xs to the empty string. RESULT xs]
            [COMMAND If lm is empty or whitespace after stripping, return ZERO ONLY; otherwise return lm.strip(), followed by a space, xs, and ONLY. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.trans_two:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Convert a numeric string into the English word form for its two-digit value by left-padding to width 2 and handling single digits, teens, exact tens, and general tens-plus-ones cases." trans_two]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> s </REF>: string "Numeric string to convert, expected to contain digits and treated as a two-digit value after left-padding with zeros to length 2."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "English word representation selected from number lookup tables based on the padded two-digit value."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Left-pad s with zeros to a minimum width of 2 using zfill(2), overwriting s with the padded string. RESULT s]
            [COMMAND If the first character of s is "0", return self.NUMBER indexed by the integer value of the last character of s. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise, if the first character of s is "1", return self.NUMBER_TEEN indexed by integer(s) minus 10. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise, if the second character of s is "0", return self.NUMBER_TEN indexed by the integer value of the first character of s minus 1. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise, return self.NUMBER_TEN indexed by the integer value of the first character of s minus 1, followed by a space, followed by self.NUMBER indexed by the integer value of the last character of s. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The padded string s has first character equal to "0".]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Treat the value as a single-digit number and return only the ones-word lookup for the last digit. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The padded string s has first character equal to "1" after the first condition did not match.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Treat the value as a teen number from 10 through 19 and return the teen-word lookup using integer(s) minus 10. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The padded string s has second character equal to "0" after the first two conditions did not match.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Treat the value as an exact multiple of ten and return only the tens-word lookup for the first digit minus 1. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: None of the earlier conditions matched, meaning the tens digit is neither "0" nor "1" and the ones digit is not "0".]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Construct the result as the tens-word lookup, then a single space, then the ones-word lookup. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.trans_three:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Convert a three-character numeric string into words by delegating leading-zero cases to the two-digit converter, emitting exact hundreds without a suffix, and otherwise appending the translated last two digits after 'HUNDRED AND'." trans_three]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> s </REF>: string "A three-character numeric string to translate into words."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "The word-form translation of the input numeric string."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether the first character of s is equal to "0". RESULT is_leading_zero]
            [COMMAND If is_leading_zero is true, return the result of calling self.trans_two on the substring s[1:] and stop further processing. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND If the first character of s is not "0", check whether the substring s[1:] is exactly equal to "00". RESULT is_exact_hundred]
            [COMMAND If is_exact_hundred is true, convert s[0] to an integer, use it to index self.NUMBER, concatenate the selected word with " HUNDRED", return that string, and stop further processing. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND If the first character of s is not "0" and s[1:] is not "00", convert s[0] to an integer, use it to index self.NUMBER, call self.trans_two on s[1:], concatenate the hundreds word with " HUNDRED AND " and the translated suffix, and return the final string. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The first character of s is equal to "0".]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the result of self.trans_two called with s[1:]. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The first character of s is not "0" and the substring s[1:] is exactly "00".]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the word for the first digit from self.NUMBER indexed by int(s[0]) followed by " HUNDRED". RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The first character of s is not "0" and the substring s[1:] is not "00".]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the word for the first digit from self.NUMBER indexed by int(s[0]) followed by " HUNDRED AND " and the result of self.trans_two called with s[1:]. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.parse_more:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Return the element from self.NUMBER_MORE selected by the input index or key i." parse_more]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> i </REF>: index_or_key "Selector used to access an element from self.NUMBER_MORE."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: any "The value retrieved from self.NUMBER_MORE at index or key i."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Access self.NUMBER_MORE using i as the index or key and retrieve the selected value. RESULT selected_value]
            [COMMAND Return the retrieved value to the caller. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
